sections.html:
Pressed against the Kansas border, Cass County is part of greater Kansas City, with Harrisonville as its courthouse town. The county has grown to 115,859 people (July 2025), a 7.5% gain on 2020, and 75.6% of its homes have owners living in them. New subdivisions in Belton, Raymore and Peculiar sit near resale houses, which gives an older home in Harrisonville or Pleasant Hill real competition when pricing.

MeasureCass County
Midpoint owner-occupied home value$292,400
Midpoint monthly rent$1,205
Midpoint household income$87,535
New-building permits, 2025487

Twelve school districts touch Cass, including Harrisonville R-IX, Belton, Raymore-Peculiar R-II, Pleasant Hill R-III, Archie R-V and Lee's Summit R-VII. Schools, fire protection and the library each levy separately. Equal assessed values therefore don't guarantee equal bills, and the district names on your statement show why.

The two offices sit side by side on Cantrell Road in Harrisonville.

  • Collector: 2725 Cantrell Road, 816-380-8377, collector@casscounty.com. Counter service runs Monday to Friday, eight to four-thirty.
  • Assessor: 2733 Cantrell Road, 816-380-8400.
  • County Clerk: Historic Courthouse, 102 E. Wall Street. The Clerk handles the paperwork for the Board of Equalization.

A drop box for the Collector is at Annex 1, 201 W. Wall Street, and anything placed in it before midnight on December 31 counts as on time. Property tax is not paid at the Treasurer's office, and deeds are filed with the Recorder of Deeds. Search records or print a receipt through casscountycollector.org.

Once your real estate statement arrives, you may pay it, and the hard stop is December 31. The county mails statements during November. A mailed check is judged by its U.S. Postal Service postmark, and metered postage from a private machine is refused. No statement by the end of November? Phone 816-380-8377.

Starting January 1 the Collector adds penalties and fees, which may reach 25 percent in the first delinquent year. A bill that never showed up doesn't excuse the debt. Tax is a claim on the land itself, so the next owner inherits any unpaid amount.

Statements carry whatever owner and address are on file when they print. A sale closing in October or later can therefore produce a bill in the old owner's name. If that is you, hand the Collector the buyer's name and mailing address. A buyer with nothing in hand by December 10 should call.

sections.h2: How the tax bill is figured
sections.html:
The bill comes from two things: the Assessor's value, and the levy from every taxing body covering the parcel. Divide assessed value by 100, then multiply by the combined rate.

  • Homes and other residential property: 19 percent of market value
  • Commercial property: 32 percent
  • Farm ground: 12 percent

Every odd-numbered year the county updates values across the board, while new construction is added when finished. If levies fall, a higher value may still leave your bill unchanged, and levies are normally set in September. Whether Cass offers the homestead credit in RSMo 137.1050 is a question for the Assessor at 816-380-8400, so ask before assuming it applies to the home you're selling.

sections.h2: How to appeal a Cass County value
sections.html:
Only market value is up for debate. Complaining that the bill is too high won't move the Board. What does help: photographs of defects, what your property sold for recently, or an appraiser's testimony.

  1. Start by discussing the value with the Assessor's staff.
  2. Mail or deliver the Board of Equalization appeal form to the Assessor with a July postmark by the posted date.
  3. If the Board does not satisfy you, the State Tax Commission is next: file by September 30, or 30 days after the Board's last action when that is later.

The County Commission appoints Board members and the County Clerk's office processes the filings. Look for the next appeal season after the 2027 reassessment. The statutes behind this are RSMo 138.430 and RSMo 137.275.

Tax certificates are auctioned in the Harrisonville courthouse, 102 E. Wall Street, starting at 10 a.m. on August's fourth Monday. Expect the next one in August 2027. Land becomes eligible when its real estate tax is still unpaid after March 1 of the year after it was billed. RSMo 140.150 fixes the sale day and has the Collector notify the record owner before the list is published.

Owners may settle the back tax, penalty, interest and costs before the auction, and the Collector's website has a section for bidders. For a seller, a listing is a deadline. Paying the balance at closing removes the parcel.

Behind on tax and ready to sell? Ask the Collector for the precise balance with penalty and interest, then pass it to the title company so it appears on the settlement statement. Once paid, the parcel falls off any certificate sale list.

Gather three things before you list: the parcel number from your latest statement, the Collector's payoff figure, and the name of your lender if it escrows. With those in hand the title company can order the payoff letters without delay and your closing date won't hinge on a tax question.

Afterward, give the Collector the new owner's name and mailing address so November's statement goes to the right mailbox. A bill that still reaches you for a sold house should be forwarded along with those details, not paid out of your own pocket.

Closing usually splits the year's tax, with the buyer credited for each month or day you owned the home. The Collector receives nothing at the table. The buyer later pays the whole annual bill by December 31. A lender that escrows your tax should hear about the payoff, since it normally refunds the cushion or applies it to the loan.

The Recorder's FAQ promises same-day to 24-hour turnaround on real estate recordings, skipping weekends and holidays. Recorded deeds show no sale price. Staff there won't phone out closing details or search for liens, so lean on the title company, because liens can also sit with the courts or the Collector.

Cash Home Buyers works with Cass County owners who have unpaid tax, a tenant, an inherited house or deferred repairs, and can give a written offer after seeing the property. There is no lender to wait for, so closing can move at your pace.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Cass County property tax?
faqs.a: Bring it to the Collector at 2725 Cantrell Road in Harrisonville, weekdays. The drop box at 201 W. Wall Street counts until midnight on December 31, and casscountycollector.org lets you view bills online.

faqs.q: What does a late payment cost?
faqs.a: Penalties and fees can climb to 25 percent during the first year of delinquency, starting after December 31. By mail, only a U.S. postmark of December 31 or earlier keeps you on time.

faqs.q: Who covers the tax at closing, the buyer or the seller?
faqs.a: The year's tax is generally split, with the buyer credited for the stretch the seller owned the house. The Collector gets no money at closing, and the buyer pays the entire bill by December 31.

faqs.q: When does the county auction tax certificates?
faqs.a: Every August on the fourth Monday, 10 a.m., at the courthouse, 102 E. Wall Street, Harrisonville. Land can be offered if its real estate tax is still open after March 1 of the next year.

faqs.q: What is the first step to dispute my value?
faqs.a: Phone the Assessor at 816-380-8400. If that fails, send the Board of Equalization form to the same office with a July postmark by the deadline, and take any remaining dispute to the State Tax Commission.
